candidate_relations.reason: C001 names the identical diagnostic entity as the reference — congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris — with all required components (congenital onset, unilateral, hypoplasia, specific muscle). The clinical record supports this: isolated right lower lip deviation on movement with symmetric rest appearance and normal neuroimaging/cardiac workup.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Exact match: congenital, unilateral, hypoplasia, depressor anguli oris muscle

candidate_relations.reason: Congenital lower lip palsy is the functional/clinical description of the presentation and is compatible with the reference diagnosis, but it lacks the required specificity of muscle hypoplasia as the etiology, making it a parent/phenotypic label rather than the complete diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Describes the clinical phenotype (lower lip palsy) but does not specify the anatomical substrate (depressor anguli oris hypoplasia)

candidate_relations.reason: Peripheral seventh nerve palsy would be expected to produce weakness across multiple facial muscle groups (forehead, eye closure, nasolabial fold), but the examination explicitly shows these are symmetric. The isolated lower lip deviation with normal neuroimaging points to a muscle-level defect, not a nerve palsy, making this an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Peripheral CN VII palsy implies broader facial nerve dysfunction; the record shows isolated lower lip deviation with all other facial movements intact

case_quality_flags: Classic teaching case for congenital depressor anguli oris hypoplasia; normal cardiac echo and MRI appropriately exclude syndromic associations (e.g., CHARGE, DiGeorge) and central/peripheral nerve etiologies.
